entries.title: Five Music Autobiographies That Are Candid About Their Struggles
entries.summary: These memoirs not only tell fascinating stories about life in the music industry but also demonstrate that recovery, resilience and personal growth are possible, even after periods of immense difficulty. The post Five Music Autobiographies That Are Candid About Their Struggles first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Music stars often appear larger than life, filling stadiums, topping the charts and enjoying glamorous lifestyles. Yet behind the fame, many artists have battled deeply personal challenges, including addiction, mental health issues, trauma and the pressures of life in the spotlight. In recent years, a growing number of musicians have chosen to share these experiences honestly through autobiographies, offering readers an unfiltered look at both their successes and their setbacks.

These memoirs not only tell fascinating stories about life in the music industry but also demonstrate that recovery, resilience and personal growth are possible, even after periods of immense difficulty.

1. The Heroin Diaries by Nikki Sixx

The Heroin Diaries is one of the most raw and uncompromising autobiographies ever written by a rock musician. Based on the journals kept by Nikki Sixx during the late 1980s, the book chronicles the height of his heroin addiction and the chaos that surrounded his life.

Rather than glorifying substance misuse, Sixx vividly describes the devastating impact addiction had on his health, relationships and career. He recounts overdoses, reckless behaviour and the emotional emptiness that accompanied fame.

What makes the autobiography particularly powerful is its honesty. Sixx openly reflects on the mistakes he made while explaining how recovery allowed him to rebuild both his personal life and his career.

2. Life by Keith Richards

Life by Keith Richards offers far more than tales of rock-and-roll excess. While the memoir certainly covers the legendary lifestyle associated with The Rolling Stones, it also explores the realities behind decades of substance use and intense public scrutiny.

Richards writes candidly about addiction, creative partnerships and the pressures of global fame, acknowledging both the highs and the consequences of his lifestyle.

The autobiography balances humour with self-reflection, giving readers an honest account of one of rock music’s most enduring figures.

3. Scar Tissue by Anthony Kiedis

Scar Tissue sees Anthony Kiedis recount a lifetime of addiction, recovery and resilience.

Kiedis describes growing up in an unconventional environment where drugs were introduced at a young age before following him into adulthood and throughout his career with Red Hot Chili Peppers.

The memoir details repeated attempts at drug addiction treatment and sobriety, periods of relapse, and the emotional toll addiction took on friendships and relationships. At the same time, it highlights how creativity and determination helped him continue making music while working towards recovery.

It remains one of the most honest accounts of addiction written by a modern rock musician.

4. Broken Music by Sting

Unlike some of the more dramatic rock memoirs, Broken Music by Sting takes a reflective approach to life’s struggles.

Rather than focusing primarily on addiction, Sting writes openly about grief, family difficulties, uncertainty and the emotional pressures that accompanied his rise from a working-class upbringing to international success with The Police.

His thoughtful storytelling demonstrates that personal struggles come in many forms and that emotional resilience often develops over many years.

Readers looking for a more introspective autobiography will find plenty of insight throughout this memoir.

5. Born to Run by Bruce Springsteen

Born to Run is an exceptionally honest memoir by Bruce Springsteen, who speaks openly about depression, anxiety and the emotional challenges that existed despite his enormous success.

Springsteen explores how childhood experiences shaped his adult life and discusses his decision to seek professional help for his mental health.

Rather than presenting himself as a flawless rock icon, he offers a deeply human account of vulnerability, perseverance and the importance of asking for support when needed.

His willingness to discuss mental health has been widely praised and has encouraged many readers to have more open conversations about their own wellbeing.

entries.title: Kobo CEO Michael Tamblyn Banned from Instagram Threads
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo CEO Michael Tamblyn has just been banned from Meta's Instagram Threads. The post Kobo CEO Michael Tamblyn Banned from Instagram Threads first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo CEO Michael Tamblyn has just been banned from Meta’s Instagram Threads. He frequently uses the platform to answer customer questions about Kobo e-readers, explain company logistics, and engage with the broader reading community. While Threads has recently experienced an uptick in automated AI moderation, resulting in accidental account suspensions for some high-profile creators, Tamblyn’s account is now banned, and it is unknown whether it will be unbanned anytime soon.

Threads is a text-focused social media app built by Meta’s Instagram team that lets users share short updates, photos, and videos in public conversations. Posts can include up to 500 characters of text, links, photos, and videos up to 5 minutes long. Users can reply to posts, repost content, quote others, and like updates, much like other microblogging platforms.

entries.title: Here is the The Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist
entries.summary: The Booker Prize 2026 shortlist of six novels was officially announced on September 22, 2026. The judging panel described the final selections as deeply "human" narratives that artificial intelligence cannot replicate. The post Here is the The Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist was announced on September 22, 2026, featuring six nominated books chosen by a judging panel chaired by classicist and writer Mary Beard. Each year, the prize is awarded to what is, in the opinion of the judges, the best sustained work of fiction written in English and published in the UK and Ireland. The winning book is a work that not only speaks to our current times, but will also endure and join the pantheon of great literature.

The winner and the shortlisted authors are guaranteed a global readership and a life-changing increase in book sales. The winner of the Booker Prize also receives £50,000, with £2,500 awarded to each of the other shortlisted authors. The grand prize will be announced on November 9th in London.

The Disappearers: A Novel

entries.title: iReader Air 3 Pro Boyuan is now available
entries.summary: The iReader Air 3 Pro "Boyuan" edition is an 8.2-inch E Ink e-reader and e-note device featuring an ultra-slim 5.4mm metallic frame, physical page-turn buttons, and high-performance specs. The post iReader Air 3 Pro Boyuan is now available first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The iReader Air 3 Pro “Boyuan” edition is an 8.2-inch E Ink e-reader and e-note device featuring an ultra-slim 5.4mm metallic frame, physical page-turn buttons, and high-performance specs. This new model is an improved version of the Air 3 Pro, which launched in August. This is a Chinese exclusive and will retail for around $420.00.

This e-reader features an 8.2-inch E Ink Carta 1300 screen with a resolution of 300 PPU and 00 PPI class, and up to a 50 fps refresh rate. The e-reader offers responsive e-paper generation with significantly darker blacks and higher contrast. This model has a traditional front-lit display, with warm and cool lights.

The device integrates physical page-turn buttons along the side bezel, making it highly ergonomic for single-handed reading. It includes an electromagnetic stylus for sketching, note-taking, and direct annotation of PDFs or e-books. The device offers expandable storage, giving it an edge over competing devices with locked internal storage capacities.

Under the hood is an 8-core CPU, 4GB of RAM, and 64 GB of internal storage. A dedicated microSD slot supports up to 2 TB of external storage. Runs Android-based SmartOS, though iReader’s stock interface is tailored primarily for the Chinese domestic market and does not have Google Play; users will be able to install their own apps.

It remains to be seen whether this will be released internationally as the Ocean series. If it does come out on Amazon, I’ll report on it. In the meantime, it is available to order from JD.

entries.title: US e-book revenues were down 3.4% in July 2026
entries.summary: The United States Publishing Industry is up 14.0% for the Month of July and up 5.4% Year-To-Date. The post US e-book revenues were down 3.4% in July 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E-book revenue in the United States fell 3.4% to $85.3 million for the month, while Digital Audiobook revenues rose 12.4% to $103.1 million. Physical Audio revenues were up 36.7% to $400 thousand. Year-to-date e-book revenues were down 3.1% compared to 2025, totaling $601.4 million. Digital Audiobook revenue was up 12.6% to $700.9 million, while Physical Audio revenue was down 8.0% to $3.1 million.

Hardback revenues were up 18.5%, coming in at $242.5 million; Paperbacks were up 25.2%, with $311.6 million in revenue; Mass Market was down 43.7% to $5.8 million; and Special Bindings were down 1.0%, with $20.6 million in revenue. Year-to-date Hardback revenues were up 1.4% year-to-date, coming in at $1.8 billion; Paperbacks were up 10.8%, with $2.0 billion in revenue; Mass Market was down 62.7% to $20.7 million; and Special Bindings were up 16.3%, with $132.1 million in revenue.

AAP StatShot reports the monthly and yearly net revenue of publishing houses from U.S. sales to bookstores, wholesalers, direct-to-consumer, online retailers, and other channels. StatShot draws revenue data from more than 1,416 publishers.

entries.title: Webcomics are winning over Gen Z
entries.summary: Readers enjoy webcomics more than top celebrities: 80% of readers love/like webcomics, a share higher than that of beloved celebrities. Zendaya, Lady Gaga, and Pedro Pascal. The post Webcomics are winning over Gen Z first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
WEBTOON turned mobile comics into a global habit for ~155 million readers, and today we’ve got the data on why that fandom runs so deep. New insights from WEBTOON, out this morning, go inside the passion driving webcomics and how the format is becoming the next cultural force out of Asia.

A new study from WEBTOON and National Research Group reveals that webcomics are doing what few forms of entertainment can: getting Gen Z to focus. The research also dives into how the format has evolved into a global cultural phenomenon, its growing influence on pop culture, and the behaviors that define its deeply passionate fandom.

What began as a Korean storytelling innovation has grown into a global force across pop culture and the creator economy. With approximately 155 million monthly active users, WEBTOON Entertainment has built a vast, deeply engaged global audience, and its on-platform stories are increasingly becoming source material for hit adaptations across film, television, animation, and more.

  • Readers enjoy webcomics more than top celebrities: 80% of readers love/like webcomics, a share higher than that of beloved celebrities like. Zendaya (72%), Lady Gaga (70%), and Pedro Pascal (59%).
  • Focused Attention: Webcomic fans are deeply engaged. Half of readers (50%) browse social media less when reading webcomics, the biggest drop of any activity tested, ahead of YouTube (46%), gaming (42%), streaming (41%).

Some of the insights revealed by the study include:

The No. 1 Fandom

When readers dive into webcomics, they fall hard. Among monthly readers surveyed, 80% say they love or like webcomics—emerging as their most-loved fandom, ahead of the likes of Zendaya (72%), Lady Gaga (70%), or Pedro Pascal (59%).

From Fleeting Attention to Focused Engagement

Attention is becoming scarcer than ever, as the average person’s attention span has slipped to around 47 seconds, down from about 75 seconds a decade ago.* Yet, webcomics command attention in two important ways: sustained focus and repeated engagement. A notable 90% of readers often choose to read webcomics over other entertainment activities. In fact, half of webcomic readers (50%) browse social media less while reading webcomics—the biggest drop of any activity measured, comfortably ahead of watching YouTube (46%), gaming (42%), and TV streaming (41%).

The Return of Appointment Viewing

Streaming spent a decade teaching audiences to binge, but webcomics got Gen Z to wait for the next episode again and to enjoy it. Readers aged 13-17 rank “It feels like an event when a new episode drops” and “The wait builds suspense” among their favorite parts of a weekly release. Appointment reading but in an on-demand world, webcomic fans are choosing to return to the platform for their favorite stories.

From Page to Screen

Webcomic fans don’t want to stop at the last panel. More than 80% are excited to watch animated adaptations of the webcomics they love, 78% want to play video games based on them, and 75% plan to buy merchandise from the stories they love. For WEBTOON, that appetite starts with an original story from a Creator on the platform and grows as fans follow the story into K-Dramas, anime, and beyond.

Better Together

Webcomics turn a solo read into a shared fandom: 79% of readers enjoy talking about webcomics with others, and 77% say the format gives them something to bond over—arguably the same connection and community that helped the rise of trends like anime. Younger readers are the most likely to connect over it.

“Webcomics have built one of the most engaged fandoms in entertainment,” said Yongsoo Kim, President of WEBTOON Entertainment. “These insights show that when readers find a story they love, they give it their full attention, stay engaged, and want to come along for the journey. The deep connection that fans form with the stories they love is what sets webcomics apart, turning the format into a powerful force in pop culture.”

“Our research shows that webcomics are poised to be the next artistic import that becomes a cultural phenomenon, like anime and K-pop,” said Fergus Navaratnam-Blair, Vice President, Trends and Futures, NRG. “Based on our new research, webcomics fans are a clearly meaningful entertainment demographic. The creativity, format, and release cadence unique to the medium are all helping drive the next big wave of fandom.”

entries.title: Have you bought a Kobo e-reader from Best Buy?
entries.summary: Who needs to touch grass? Experience Kobo IRL in over 500 Best Buy retail locations across the United States. The post Have you bought a Kobo e-reader from Best Buy? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo began selling its e-readers at Best Buy retail stores and online in the United States. This began in August 2026, and we were the first to break the story. Customers have found that visiting a store and trying demo units helps them decide whether the device is right for them. Have you purchased a Kobo from Best Buy yet?

Book lovers across the United States can visit their local Best Buy to experience Kobo’s immersive reading technology firsthand. Customers can now browse, touch and purchase a range of Kobo products, including the compact, waterproof Kobo Clara Colour and Kobo Clara BW, the feature-rich, versatile Kobo Libra Colour and Kobo’s best-in-class accessories, such as Kobo Stylus 2 and Kobo Remote.

“Many readers want to be able to pick up a device, see the screen, and feel it in their hands before they commit. With Kobo eReaders now available at Best Buy, more American customers can do just that,” said Michael Tamblyn, CEO, Rakuten Kobo. “But the real magic happens once they get it home. We’ve built our e-readers to be an open, distraction-free space where the reader is in control. Whether that means endless reading with Kobo Plus, browsing our beautiful bookstore, seamless library borrowing with Libby, choosing a device with physical page-turn buttons, or simply enjoying an ad-free experience, we’re focused on making sure Kobo devices work exactly the way you want them to. We’re excited to make it easier for every kind of reader to find that right fit—an avid reader who wants to carry their entire library wherever they go, or someone looking for a more affordable, convenient way to get lost in a story.”

This retail expansion reinforces Kobo’s commitment to growing its footprint and supporting the global reading community. Whether you are a dedicated bookworm or looking for the perfect gift for a reader, the latest Kobo eReaders are now ready for pickup at a Best Buy near you.

For more information on Kobo e-readers or to find a participating Best Buy location, visit here.

entries.title: What is the Audible BOGO Sale?
entries.summary: Audible runs BOGO sales every few months. What is a BOGO sale? How does it work? What do you need to do to get audiobook discounts? The post What is the Audible BOGO Sale? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible audiobooks are digital voice recordings of books that you listen to instead of reading, provided by Audible, the world’s largest producer and retailer of audiobooks and spoken-word entertainment. Owned by Amazon, the service allows you to stream or download audiobooks, podcasts, and exclusive audio content directly to your smartphone, tablet, computer, or Amazon Echo device.

Every couple of months, Audible has a BOGO sale for audiobooks. What is a BOGO sale? An Audible BOGO sale (often called the 2-for-1 Credit Sale) is a recurring, member-only promotion that lets you buy two audiobooks for the price of one credit. Instead of spending one credit per book, your single membership credit covers both titles.

To participate, you must be an active subscriber to an Audible Premium Plus or Premium plan and have at least one available credit in your account. The sale does not apply to the entire Audible store. Instead, Audible curates a specific promotional page featuring hundreds of eligible books across various genres.

You must select two books from the designated sale list. When you add the first title to your promotional cart, the system will prompt you to add a second. Once both are in your cart, you check out using a single credit. Just like regular credit purchases, any books you buy during a BOGO sale belong to you forever, even if you eventually cancel your membership.

You can view the various BOGO sales on the Audible BOGO page. You can bookmark it, and it updates regularly with new titles every couple of months.

entries.title: CloudLibrary is coming to Kobo e-Readers
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo is running a trial period for select Canadian and US libraries using CloudLibrary with Send to Kobo. The post CloudLibrary is coming to Kobo e-Readers first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
CloudLibrary is a platform libraries use to manage their e-book and audiobook collections, similar to Overdrive Libby. CloudLibrary and Kobo appear to be working on an integration that is undergoing a trial period with select libraries in September, with a broader rollout to the Kobo Clara Color, Kobo Clara BW, and Kobo Libra Color in October.

In the CloudLibrary app or on the website, click Send to Kobo next to a title to borrow it and send it to your Kobo eReader. You can also borrow CloudLibrary books from various libraries’ online catalogs. But the ‘Send to Kobo’ button is only available in the CloudLibrary app or on the website, so you will need to go there to send anything to your Kobo. The trial also works only with e-books, not audiobooks.

It remains to be seen if Kobo will include a CloudLibrary system similar to Libby, where you can browse your local branch’s online catalog right on the e-reader and attach your card in the settings menu. It is unlikely that you will be able to attach more than one CloudLibrary account on the Kobo e-reader.

Here are some tips about the beta

  • The borrowed book will be removed from the Kobo upon its expiry date.
  • If a book is renewed in the CloudLibrary app or website it must be sent to the Kobo again.
  • If you read the book on the CloudLibrary app or website in addition to reading it on the Kobo, your reading position will not be synchronized with the Kobo.
  • A CloudLibrary account can only be connected to one Kobo account.

entries.title: Tapmora E INK Fridge Magnet Review
entries.summary: Whether it’s a goofy snapshot of your pet, a breathtaking view from your last road trip, or a daily motivational quote to start your morning—Tapmora makes your space uniquely yours. The post Tapmora E INK Fridge Magnet Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Tapmora is an electronics brand best known for creating the world’s first battery-free E Ink Photo Magnet. The device is a cordless, pocket-sized digital frame that lets users instantly transfer smartphone photos to a paper-like, magnetic display without charging cables, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth. It retails for $45 and is available to order from the company’s website.

The Tapmora E Ink Photo Magnet offers a clever, low-maintenance way to display digital memories without the clutter of charging cables. Its standout feature is NFC energy harvesting, letting users push photos directly from a smartphone app with a simple tap. Reviewers note that using the Spectra 6 full-color array pays off significantly; unlike cheaper 4-color portable panels that turn vibrant landscapes or skin tones into muddy grays, Tapmora preserves color accuracy and rich tones. The passive, matte, paper-like display blends smoothly into refrigerators or desks, offering a premium “printed” aesthetic that feels much more organic than a harsh, glowing LCD screen.

However, the tech comes with clear trade-offs, depending on your expectations. Because the screen relies entirely on a temporary burst of electricity harvested from your phone’s NFC chip, image transfers take a few seconds, and the device lacks backlighting or built-in buttons for manual refreshes. While it aligns with the industry’s shift toward pocket-sized magnetic smart tiles, it operates strictly as a static canvas rather than a responsive gadget. Ultimately, it is a beautifully packaged niche novelty that offers great value for anyone looking to ditch instant film or static prints, though it may not fully satisfy tech enthusiasts seeking interactive functionality.
